notes: Example configuration generated by the CraneCalc configurator; fictitious crane, supplier, survey and owner data, to be replaced with project data. Scope: 4 simply supported 25-ft bays, W21X101 girders, one 10-ton pendant crane, on new welded haunched rib seats welded to the existing W14X120 columns, with the rail, ties, bearings and end stops; the existing columns are checked with their existing load effects and the existing sidewall rod bracing takes the crane longitudinal forces. A direct flange saddle does not suit this rolled girder (the sized saddle leaves saddle-across-fatigue 4.54, flange-tie-flange 1.43 for the estimated tie demands; a welded saddle is a Category D/E attachment on the top flange of this high-cycle runway (CMAA Class D, AIST Class A)): the paired flat bars bolt to the tie-side bearing stiffener, cut as one plate with its gusset extension past the flange tip (no weld at the gusset), the full-depth stiffener pair carrying the tie force into the girder. Bumper overhang assumed 20 in (end-wheel centerline to the extended bumper face, a typical supplier proportion): the stop contact positions use it; confirm with the crane supplier.

aist.cycleSource: Fictitious example duty: 2,000,000 crane passages in three duty bins (rated, half and light lifts), loaded and empty passes included. selections.reason: A direct flange saddle does not suit this rolled girder (the sized saddle leaves saddle-across-fatigue 4.54, flange-tie-flange 1.43 for the estimated tie demands; a welded saddle is a Category D/E attachment on the top flange of this high-cycle runway (CMAA Class D, AIST Class A)): the paired flat bars bolt to the tie-side bearing stiffener, cut as one plate with its gusset extension past the flange tip (no weld at the gusset), the full-depth stiffener pair carrying the tie force into the girder.

Lightest compact W within the sizing targets (ratio ≤ 0.85, deflections ≤ 0.9 of the limits): screening estimates, top-flange tip stress (DG7, warping and second-order twist) ratio 0.78, vertical deflection 0.70, lateral 0.43 and rail-head movement with twist 0.68 of their limits; flanges at least 216 mm wide for the end bearing bolt gauge and the rail seat; lighter candidates rejected: 21 by sizing ratio, 42 by flange width; the next lighter, W16X100: tips ratio 0.91 > 0.85; vertical deflection 1.14 of the limit > 0.9. These are the configurator's screening estimates (a simplified model that ranks the catalog), not the final ratios: the calculation checks the section and reports its own ratios.
Fictitious example existing column for a 10-ton crane (W14X90 to 7.5 t, W14X120 to 15 t, W14X159 to 30 t, else W14X211); replace with the surveyed shape.

Weld-on clip bases on the top flange are an AISC Table A-3.1 item 7.1 attachment, Category D: the estimated top-plate range 91.6 MPa (rated-lift crane moment without impact plus the top-flange lateral bending under the side thrust) at all 2,000,000 cycles exceeds F_SR = 71.2 MPa (ratio 1.29, the project's all-cycle method). Bolted clamp plates leave holes for pretensioned bolts (item 2.2, Category B), as AISC DG7 and AIST TR-13 allow.

fabrication.steel: Girder ASTM A992; plates, bars and stiffeners ASTM A572 Grade 50 unless noted.
fabrication.bolting: ASTM F3125 Grade A325, pretensioned, Class B faying surfaces, standard holes unless slots are detailed. Sliding-end bearing bolts and column-end tie bolts pretensioned against steel sleeves. Rail joints thermite or flash-butt welded by the rail supplier's qualified procedure (preheat, grinding, inspection); no joint bars or bolts.
fabrication.welding: E70XX low-hydrogen electrodes per AWS D1.1/D1.1M:2020, cyclically loaded provisions. Continuous fillets as dimensioned; no intermittent welds on cyclic load paths. Smooth starts and stops.
fabrication.inspection: Visual inspection of all welds; AWS D1.1/D1.1M:2020 cyclically loaded acceptance criteria; magnetic particle testing of fillets at fatigue-sensitive attachments; 100% ultrasonic testing of CJP welds; bolt pretension verification per RCSC.
fabrication.erection: Set and level the bearings, install the end bearings and flange ties, then set the rails. Provide temporary restraint until the permanent ties are complete.
fabrication.railAlignment: Set the rails to the specified gauge, alignment and level tolerances and survey them after erection, before the load test.
